trial_title: Clomiphene Citrate for the Treatment of Low Testosterone Associated With Chronic Opioid Pain Medication Administration
brief_summary:
The purpose of this randomized controlled clinical trial is to evaluate the effects of clomiphene citrate compared to placebo (substance without active medication) in men who are taking pain medication (opioids) for chronic pain conditions and who have low blood testosterone levels.

eligibility_table.criterion: Low testosterone as defined by criteria (serum total testosterone <350 ng/dl in men <55 years, <300 ng/dl in men 55-65 years)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's serum testosterone level is 65 ng/dL, which is below the threshold of 350 ng/dL for men under 55 years.

eligibility_table.criterion: EITHER taking opioid pain medication (see A below) OR planning to start new pain medication regimen (see B below)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is not currently taking opioid pain medication and there is no indication of a planned new pain medication regimen.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient currently taking any opioid pain medication or planning to start a new pain medication regimen within the next month?

eligibility_table.criterion: A) EITHER continuous opioid treatment for chronic nonmalignant pain for >=6 months receiving one of several specified opioid regimens for the past 1 month (including >=20 mg/day of oral methadone, >=30 mg/day of oral sustained release oxycodone, >=30 mg/day of oral morphine sulfate, >=6 mg/day of oral dilaudid or >= 8 mg/day of dilaudid ER, or >=25 mcg/hr of transdermal fentanyl or buprenorphine, or intrathecal morphine pump)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient does not meet the criteria for continuous opioid treatment for chronic nonmalignant pain as there is no evidence of such treatment.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient been receiving continuous opioid treatment for chronic nonmalignant pain for at least 6 months, with a current regimen that includes ≥20 mg/day of oral methadone, ≥30 mg/day of oral sustained release oxycodone, ≥30 mg/day of oral morphine sulfate, ≥6 mg/day of oral dilaudid, ≥8 mg/day of dilaudid ER, ≥25 mcg/hr of transdermal fentanyl or buprenorphine, or intrathecal morphine pump?

eligibility_table.criterion: B) OR the pain management physician is planning to start pain medication (opioid or non-opioid pain therapy) but you have not received it yet. If this is the case, your testosterone will be checked before starting and during 1 month of pain therapy to determine if you have low testosterone to qualify to begin medication (clomiphene or placebo) treatment in this study.
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided that indicates the patient is planning to start a pain medication regimen.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient had a serum testosterone level checked within the last month to confirm it is ≤300 ng/dL before starting any pain therapy?

eligibility_table.criterion: Presence of clear secondary hypogonadism with hypogonadal symptoms and low total testosterone level (confirmed with morning testosterone level <= 350 ng/dL for men age >= 55 and <= 300ng/dl for men age 55-65) or total testosterone <=200 ng/dl (regardless of symptoms). Additionally luteinizing hormone (LH) should be <15 mIU (milli-International unit )/mL (at baseline only). Symptoms of hypogonadism include fatigue, decreased energy level/endurance, depressed mood, decreased libido, erectile dysfunction.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has clear secondary hypogonadism with low total testosterone level and symptoms consistent with hypogonadism.

eligibility_table.criterion: Chronic nonmalignant pain etiology includes rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, spinal stenosis, polymyalgia, complex region pain syndrome I and II, neurinoma, phantom limb pain, neuropathic pain of other origin, scoliosis, neck pain, failed back surgery, or chronic pancreatitis.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's chronic pain etiology is not specified, and thus it cannot be determined if it falls within the listed conditions.
